content.productDescription:
Bring a real sense of calm and meaning into your home with this set of three Islamic calligraphy wall art prints — genuinely one of my favourite choices for anyone looking for artwork for a living room that feels both beautiful and deeply personal. Each print pairs flowing Arabic calligraphy with soft, swirling abstract shapes in blush, dusty blue, and warm taupe tones on a clean white background, giving you that rare combination of bold lettering and gentle colour that feels peaceful rather than overwhelming.

The two designs you can see in the artwork carry Quranic verses rendered in an expressive, hand-brushed calligraphy style — one reading 'And Whatever of Blessings and Good Things You Have, It Is From Allah', and the other 'Allah Is The Light of The Heavens and The Earth'. The swirling marbled shapes behind each inscription move between soft blush pinks and muted slate blues, making the dark brown-toned Arabic script really stand out. It's a design that feels contemporary and classic at the same time — and the white background means it sits beautifully against almost any wall colour.

What's Included with Artwork for a Living Room Islamic Calligraphy "And Whatever of Blessings" & "Allah Is The Light of The Heavens and The Earth" Blue & Blush Wall Art Prints | Set of 3

  • A set of 3 Islamic calligraphy art prints featuring Quranic verses with swirling blush and blue abstract backgrounds on white
  • Printed in the UK using fade-resistant pigment inks — colours stay true for years
  • Suitable for indoor use
  • Framed and canvas-wrapped options arrive ready to hang — no hunting for a frame that fits, no hassle, just hang and enjoy
  • Choose between unframed and framed options in multiple sizes and in Luster or Museum quality; also available in wrapped canvas size options

How to Style Artwork for a Living Room with Islamic Calligraphy Prints

I'd hang all three prints in a horizontal row above the sofa at eye level, with an even gap of around five to eight centimetres between each one — it creates a really cohesive gallery feel without any fuss. The blush and dusty blue tones in these prints work especially well with warm white, soft grey, or even a deep navy accent wall, so they're very easy to work around an existing colour scheme. If your living room already has touches of natural wood, rattan or linen, these prints will feel right at home — the taupe and blush tones in the artwork pick up those natural, earthy notes beautifully.

For a more layered look, try pairing them above a sideboard or console table with a small plant and a candle in a complementary blue or cream tone. They also work well in a hallway or a reading nook if you want to spread the set around the home. For more Islamic and Muslim wall art ideas, have a browse through our Islamic wall art collection — there's plenty of inspiration in there to help you put together a look you'll love.

Choosing the Right Size and Style for Your Space

Before you pick your size, it's worth thinking about the wall space you have available. As a general rule, I'd suggest the total width of your three prints (including the gaps between them) should be roughly two thirds of the width of your sofa or the furniture piece below them — this keeps everything looking balanced and intentional rather than lost on the wall. If you have high ceilings, go a size up from what you think you need; prints often look smaller on the wall than they do on screen.

In terms of paper choice, Luster gives you a lovely gentle sheen that brings out the blush and blue tones really nicely in natural light, while Museum quality paper has a matte finish that works beautifully in rooms with stronger overhead lighting where you want to avoid any glare. Either way, the calligraphy and the swirling abstract details come through with real depth and clarity. Scroll down to see how each size looks in a living room before you decide — there's a size-guide image below showing every option in context so you can choose with confidence.

aiItems.content:
What is artwork for a living room?

Artwork for a living room is any print, canvas or framed piece chosen specifically to enhance the look and feel of your main living space. It can range from abstract colour studies and photography to calligraphy and typographic prints, and is usually displayed on a focal wall, above a sofa or as part of a gallery arrangement. The best living room artwork reflects the personality and values of the people in the home — for many Muslim households, that means Islamic calligraphy prints featuring Quranic verses or the names of Allah. Choosing the right set of prints brings colour, meaning and a finished, pulled-together look to a room that might otherwise feel incomplete.

How to Hang Artwork for a Living Room in 5 Simple Steps

1. Choose your wall: Pick a focal wall — above the sofa is the classic choice. Make sure it's a wall you see as soon as you walk into the room for maximum impact.

2. Measure your space: For a set of 3 prints, aim for a total display width of around two thirds of the sofa or furniture below. This keeps the arrangement balanced and well-proportioned.

3. Plan your layout first: Lay the prints on the floor in front of the wall before putting a single nail in. This lets you adjust spacing and order without any holes in the wrong place.

4. Hang at eye level: The centre of each print should sit roughly 145–150 cm from the floor — this is the standard gallery height and it feels natural when you're standing or sitting on the sofa.

5. Keep gaps even: For a clean, contemporary row of three, use a consistent 5–8 cm gap between each print. Use a spirit level or a long piece of string as a guide to keep everything straight.

Choosing Your Print Format: Which Option Is Right for You?

Unframed Print — The print is delivered rolled, ready for you to frame yourself. Great if you already have frames you love or want to match a very specific frame colour. Available in Luster or Museum quality paper.

Framed Print — Arrives fully assembled and ready to hang straight out of the box — no extra trips to a frame shop needed. A brilliant time-saver and the most popular choice. Available in Luster or Museum quality paper.

Wrapped Canvas — The artwork is printed directly onto canvas and stretched over a wooden frame with the image wrapping around the edges. No frame required and no glass — a relaxed, contemporary look that suits modern and casual interiors well.

Luster Paper — A semi-sheen finish that makes colours pop and is especially flattering for prints with soft, blush and blue tones like these Islamic calligraphy designs. Handles natural light beautifully.

Museum Quality Paper — A smooth, matte fine-art finish with excellent depth and detail. Ideal if you want a more refined, gallery-style look or if your room has strong overhead lighting where a sheen could cause glare.
